findings.F1: The coin's next-day excess return runs against the day's own volatility-scaled return only when 30-day volatility is high: the slope is -0.0058 (t -6.30, n 4355) in each coin's top volatility tercile, against -0.0013 (t -2.06) in the middle tercile and +0.0008 (t 1.46) in the low tercile. In the high tercile the slope is negative in all six coins (t from -0.90 for ZEC to -4.15 for XMR) and in both halves of the windows (w1-12: t -2.66, w13-24: t -5.79).
findings.F2: On down days, the heavier the volume against its 30-day average, the higher the next day's excess return. The top volume-surprise quartile of down days returns +0.0068 (t 4.85, n 1573), while the other three quartiles return -0.0004 to +0.0006. The slope on log volume surprise is positive in all six coins (0.0019 to 0.0057) and in both halves (t 2.50 and 3.71). In a joint regression the fall × volume term carries the effect (t 2.93), while the fall alone (t 1.09) and the volume alone (t 0.55) do not; on up days the volume slope has no consistent sign (-0.0040 to +0.0048).
findings.F3: The rebound after vol-scaled falls is at least as strong when the 30-day return is negative. Falls beyond 2 daily volatilities return +0.0083 (t 1.97, n 255) and falls of 1 to 2 volatilities return +0.0045 (t 2.27, n 681). The per-coin slope of the next-day return on fall size is positive in all six coins in that regime (t 0.53 to 2.66), against five of six while the 30-day return is positive.
findings.F4: Up days in high volatility while the 30-day return is negative are followed by a weak next day, -0.0070 excess (t -4.46, n 1109), while high-volatility down days in the same regime are followed by +0.0068 (t 3.78, n 1200). The reversal of F1 is concentrated in falling months.
findings.F5: The book stays mostly out of the market (mean allocation 0.10, in a position on 24% of bars) and earns 0.000219 a day. It lost less than holding in the falling years (2018: -0.00045 against -0.00349) but gave up most of the rise in the rising ones (2020: 0.00082 against 0.00423). The tested rule captures only the down-day, up-month slice of the reversal shown in F1 to F4.

ideas.idea: When a coin's 30-day daily volatility is high relative to its own usual level, the larger its latest one-day return in units of that volatility, the more its return over the next 1 day goes the opposite way, with falls followed by gains and rises followed by losses.
ideas.consequence: In a volatile market, fade the day's move in proportion to its size rather than following it.
ideas.name: high-volatility one-day reversal

ideas.idea: The larger a coin's one-day fall relative to its 30-day daily volatility, multiplied by how far that day's volume stands above its 30-day average volume, the higher the coin's return over the next 1 day.
ideas.consequence: A sharp fall on heavy volume is a reason to buy for the next day, not to sell.
ideas.name: heavy-volume selloff rebound

ideas.idea: While a coin's 30-day return is negative, the larger its latest one-day fall relative to its 30-day daily volatility, the higher its return over the next 1 day.
ideas.consequence: Do not chase a coin lower after a sharp down day in a falling month, because the next day tends to bounce.
ideas.name: down-month down-day rebound
